Use this reference to look up a YAML setting, understand which files a build
will touch, or restore a saved result. For a first build, follow the [getting started guide](get-started.html).

## The project root and profiles

Run the first build from the analysis project. If it has no base configuration,
projr creates `_projr.yml` with explicit paths for `raw-data` (`_raw_data`),
`output` (`_output`), `cache` (`_tmp`), and `docs` (`docs`). Existing scripts
using those folders can keep their paths. If your files are already elsewhere,
point the corresponding label at the existing folder. Once a base file exists,
its directory declarations determine which labels are available.

| File | When it applies |
|---|---|
| `_projr.yml` | Base configuration shared by the project. |
| `_projr-<profile>.yml` | Overrides for a named analysis or machine. |
| `_projr-local.yml` | Local overrides with highest precedence. |

Each file can live at the project root or in `.projr/config/`. When both
locations contain the same filename, the root copy wins. All relative paths in
either location start at the project root. A nested script can therefore use
the same directory labels when run in RStudio or during a build.

Select profiles with a build's `profile` argument or `PROJR_PROFILE`. For
example, `Sys.setenv(PROJR_PROFILE = "site-a,cluster")` applies both named
profiles, with the earlier name taking precedence when both specify a value.
Local overrides still win. Use `projr_yml_get()` to inspect the merged settings,
`projr_yml_get("default")` to inspect the base file, and `projr_yml_check()`
to validate the active configuration.

### Choosing the checkout for a build

The first interactive build names the full project root and asks once for
permission to run its scripts and hooks, write its configured files, and
perform the requested Git and archive operations. Configured directories
can be outside the checkout. Approval is remembered for that checkout’s
path in the user’s projr configuration directory. A fresh clone at another
path prompts again, even if it contains the same `_projr.yml`.

For unattended builds, pass the root of the checkout as `project`. Use
`projr_build(project = ".", archive_github = TRUE)` when the job starts
at that root, or pass the path to the root from another working directory.
The explicit path authorizes this invocation. Git and remote destinations
still use their own credentials.

### Files projr keeps

The `.projr/` folder belongs to the project. Git can track its configuration
and manifests so a fresh checkout knows which files belonged to a build.
The production build history goes in `.projr/BUILDLOG.md` and can be committed
with the analysis. Detailed logs for individual runs stay local in `.projr/logs/`.

A build or restore moves recognized configuration files and manifests from
the earlier `_projr/` layout. Read-only queries still work on older checkouts.
If both locations contain the same configuration filename or a manifest store,
projr stops before moving anything so you can choose which history to keep.
Existing logs in a former cache directory remain readable with
`projr_log_view(log_file = "...")`.

## Directory declarations

This example keeps incoming data and generated figures where they already live.
It also creates a deliverable containing the figures and the rendered documents.

```yaml
directories:
  raw-data:
    path: incoming/site-a
  cache:
    path: scratch
  docs:
    path: reports/rendered
  output-figures:
    path: results/figures
  output-delivery:
    path: deliverables
    include: [output-figures, docs]
```

After a production build, the included copies are under
`deliverables/output-figures/` and `deliverables/docs/`. Each copy reflects
the current source, including file removals. Other files in the receiving
directory are separate from these copies. An output can include another
assembled output. Cycles, paths that would copy a directory inside itself,
and overlapping paths that could erase an input are rejected.

For R package datasets, `projr_path_get("data", "sample.rda", safe = FALSE)`
resolves to `data/sample.rda` in the project root. The `data` label is built in
and its location is fixed. A production build copies datasets staged by
`projr_use_data(sample)` into `data/` and internal datasets into `R/sysdata.rda`.
Development builds keep staged datasets under the configured cache. If an
active directory label already uses `data/` or a subdirectory such as
`data/site-a/`, the helper reports that label before saving. Projects that
store their own files there can still build and look up those paths.

| `directories.<label>` field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `path` | Required for configurable labels. An absolute path can point outside the checkout. |
| `hash` | Include the directory in the version history. Defaults to true for raw data, outputs and docs, and false for cache. |
| `include` | On an output label, list declared raw, docs or output labels to copy under their label names. An empty list requests no includes. |
| `output` | Older source-side form. Use an output label or list to copy into those outputs, `true` for all other outputs, or `false` to skip. |
| `package` | On an output label, `true` also builds the R source package and copies it under `pkg/`. |
| `source` | Preferred restore configuration by remote type. For example, `source: {local: shared}` selects a named local destination called `shared`. |
| `license` | A license identifier such as `CC-BY`, or a mapping containing `type`, `authors` and `year`. See `vignette("directory-licenses")`. |
| `ignore` | Controls both Git and R build rules. Defaults to false for package datasets (`data`) and true for other declared directories, including `raw-data`. Accepts YAML booleans, `ignore`, `no-ignore`, or `manual`. |
| `ignore-git`, `ignore-rbuild` | Set either type separately. When `ignore` is also supplied, the choices must agree. |
| `ignore-even-if-inactive` | Defaults to true. Applies that profile’s enabled ignore types while a different profile is active. |

Use a raw, cache or output prefix when a label should participate in the
corresponding build stage, for example `raw-site-a` and `output-tables`.
Declare a cache for builds that need staging, and `docs` for collected documents.
If several cache labels are configured, the first supplies the build cache. Labels used as directory lookups need a
declared path, including `code` and `data` if your scripts use those names.
The suffix `-empty` is reserved for archive metadata.

`projr_path_get("output-figures", "plot.png")` returns a filename and creates
its parent if needed. `projr_path_get_dir("output-figures")` returns a directory.
Use `create = FALSE` for lookup only. Both accept `format = "absolute"`,
`"relative"`, or `"auto"` (the default follows the YAML path's format).
Relative results are usable from the caller's working directory.
The default `safe = TRUE` allows projr to route output and document writes to
the build's working area. Use `safe = FALSE` to address the configured final
location directly. Literal paths in your own code use R's working directory.

When refreshing ignores, projr considers each profile’s configured paths.
If any eligible profile requests a Git ignore, the project keeps that rule.
R package build ignores follow the same rule when the root has a `DESCRIPTION`.
Changing a path removes the old generated rule once its last qualifying
reference disappears. User-written rules outside the managed section stay in
place. Only paths inside the checkout generate rules, so a Windows path in an
inactive profile can coexist with a Linux checkout.

Initialization keeps the contents of an existing `.gitignore` outside the
projr-managed section, including comments, duplicate rules and exceptions.
It also adds editable defaults for R session files, `.vdoc.*`, `.DS_Store`
and `Thumbs.db`. You can delete those defaults after initialization.

## Documents, R scripts and hooks

| Setting | Selection |
|---|---|
| `build.scripts` | Ordered inputs for a production build. Also used by dev builds when `dev.scripts` is absent. |
| `dev.scripts` | Ordered inputs for a development build. The `scripts` argument to `projr_build_dev()` takes precedence. |
| `build.hooks`, `dev.hooks` | Each accepts `pre`, `post`, and `both`. Supply R script paths under the stage. Dev and production hooks are configured independently. |

A script selection accepts `.R`, `.Rmd` and `.qmd` paths or glob patterns.
To skip files, add an item such as `- exclude: reports/draft.Rmd` to either
scripts list. Each `exclude` takes one path or glob pattern. Quoted strings
such as `"!reports/draft.Rmd"` also work. Matches within a glob are
alphabetical. Exclusions apply to the selection as a whole. If every entry
is an exclusion, projr uses automatic discovery and skips the matching
files. For example, `scripts: [{exclude: scratch.R}]` builds the project first and
then runs the other top-level R scripts. In a directory without a rendering
project, the remaining documents and scripts run together alphabetically.
Overlapping globs select each file once. Repeating a literal R script or
standalone document runs it again. An explicit `scripts: []`, or `scripts = character()`
in R, skips document rendering and script execution.

For example, suppose a Quarto project has the following selection.

```yaml
build:
  scripts: [prepare.R, intro.qmd, check-data.R, results.qmd, summarise.R]
  hooks:
    post: hooks/record-build.R
```

Here `prepare.R` and `check-data.R` run first. Quarto builds `intro.qmd` and
`results.qmd` together when the selection reaches `results.qmd`. Then
`summarise.R` runs. Projr temporarily sets Quarto's `project.render` (and `book.chapters` for a
book), or Bookdown's `rmd_files`. It keeps the selected configuration
through post-build hooks, then restores the original YAML, including on failure.
For Quarto document exclusions this also covers active profile and included
configuration files inside the checkout. A Quarto book needs its index page
whenever it renders any remaining chapters.
An R-only selection runs just those scripts. Documents for a different engine
render individually in their listed positions. Choose one project configuration
when both `_quarto.yml` and `_bookdown.yml` are present.

When script selection is omitted, projr builds the Quarto or Bookdown project
using its own settings and then runs top-level R scripts alphabetically. In a
directory without a rendering project it runs top-level documents and scripts
together in alphabetical order. Automatic R discovery skips configured hooks,
underscore-prefixed scripts and `renv_repos.R`.

Renderers retain their own working-directory conventions, including Quarto's
`execute-dir` and R Markdown's `knit_root_dir`. Pass native renderer arguments
through `args_engine` when needed. The collected document and its companion
assets stay together. Where basenames collide, projr preserves the affected
documents’ project-relative subdirectories. Renderer intermediates such as
generated TeX files receive project-relative ignore rules, including for
nested source documents.

## Builds, dependencies and versions

| Setting | Values and effect |
|---|---|
| `build.renv` | `auto` (default) snapshots when the project has `renv.lock` or `renv/activate.R`. `true` requests snapshots even for a first lockfile. `false` disables build snapshots. A production build checks dependencies before rendering and snapshots again without prompting afterward. |
| `build.git` | A boolean, or a mapping with booleans `commit`, `add-untracked`, and `push`. The first build writes `false` when there is no Git checkout, or disables push when the branch has no upstream. For an existing configuration with these settings omitted the normal production defaults enable all three. |
| `build.restrictions.branch` | `true` allows any branch (default), a name or list allows those branches, and `false` or `[]` allows none. |
| `build.restrictions.not_behind` | Defaults to true. Checks whether the local branch is behind its upstream before a versioned build. |
| `build.cite` | A boolean or a mapping of booleans `cff`, `inst-citation`, and `codemeta`. Selects citation files for production build updates. |
| `metadata.version-format` | Defaults to `major.minor.patch-dev`. Supported formats also allow `major.minor` or `major` before the development component, a dot separator before it, and a final `1` or `9000` in place of `dev`. |
| `parameters` | Project-specific values available inside scripts, for example `parameters: {seed: 42}` and `projr_par_get("seed")`. |

Use `projr_build_dev()` to iterate. It preserves the current project version
and can run before the project has one. An unversioned project stages its
working files in `<cache>/projr/dev/`. The `@version` placeholder requires
a version set by a production build or by `projr_version_set()`.
Use `old_dev_remove = FALSE` to keep older working directories.
Use `projr_build_patch()`, `projr_build_minor()` or `projr_build_major()` to
choose the component for a versioned build. `msg` records a build description.
`clear_output` accepts `"pre"`, `"post"` or `"never"`. Production builds default to `"pre"` and development
builds to `"never"`. Pass `clear_output = NULL` to read `PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT`. For console and file logging, profile
environment files, and authentication, see `vignette("environment")`.

If you add a package `DESCRIPTION` to an existing renv analysis, renv can
choose a new library when the next R session starts. When that library is
empty apart from renv, builds reuse the populated analysis library for this
checkout. The build and its renderers use the same packages. A populated new
library takes precedence, and explicit renv library settings are respected.
A missing renderer dependency stops the build with the package names and the
installation command for the project library.

## Hashing and history

```yaml
settings:
  hashing:
    approach: cpp
    cores: 1
```

`cpp` streams files through the native implementation. `legacy` uses the
historical R hashing method. Both produce the same file MD5s and use the same
directory histories. `cores` is a positive integer. Increase it to distribute
files across workers during a hashing phase. The default uses a single worker. The earlier `settings.hash-engine` spelling
is accepted for compatibility.

Each production build records its selected inputs before rendering and its
outputs afterward. Each directory has its own history. For example, a change
in `output` adds a new file list for that directory while `raw-data` can keep
using its existing list. Development builds leave these histories alone.

| Where to look | Where the history for `raw-data` lives |
|---|---|
| Project checkout | `.projr/manifests/raw-data/` |
| Local archive | `manifests/raw-data/` inside the archive folder |
| GitHub Release | The `raw-data/` directory inside the `manifest.zip` asset |

Open `versions.csv` in any of those directories to find a build's version,
the earliest version that recorded identical contents there, and the snapshot
identifier. The matching `files-<snapshot>.csv` lists relative filenames
and their MD5 hashes. A directory that returns to an earlier state reuses
the same list. projr can also read a legacy root `manifest.csv` and imports
its history on the next production build.

Run `projr_manifest_changes()` in the checkout to compare two builds, or
`projr_manifest_file_history()` to see when an individual file changed.
An archive records the builds it received, so its first copy of a file list
can have a different version. For a worked example with a published archive,
see [restoring an earlier build](restore-artifacts.html#when-builds-share-the-same-inputs).

## Saving artifacts

The `remotes` section was added after projr 0.6.1. To use it before
the next release, install `remotes::install_github("SATVILab/projr@main")`.

Use `remotes` to give an archive a name and record where it lives. Use
`build` to select which archives a production build writes to. This example
keeps a complete local archive called `shared` and sends just the figures to
a GitHub repository. The project declares `output-figures` under `directories`.

```yaml
remotes:
  local:
    shared:
      path: ../team-archives/study
  github:
    reports:
      repo: research-team/study-results
      tag: "figures-@branch"
      structure: archive
      send:
        cue: if-change
        inspect: manifest
        strategy: sync-diff
build:
  local:
    shared: {}
  github:
    reports:
      content: [output-figures]
```

For a name declared under `remotes`, the matching entry under `build`
has three forms.

| Entry under `build.github` or `build.local` | What a production build sends |
|---|---|
| Omit the name | Nothing to this archive. Its saved files remain available to readers. |
| `reports: {}` or a bare `reports:` | All declared raw, output and docs labels. Cache is included only when explicitly selected. |
| `reports: {content: [output-figures]}` | Only the listed labels. |

Put the address, layout and transfer settings under `remotes` and only
`content` in the matching build entry. Readers can ask for any label
actually saved for a build, even after its publishing selection changes.
Existing configurations that define a destination entirely under `build`
still work. To move an existing `build.github.archive` to the named layout,
move its address, `structure` and `send` settings to `remotes.github.archive`.
Leave its `content` selection under `build.github.archive`.

For GitHub, `repo` defaults to the repository that produced the build.
The name under `remotes.github` supplies the release tag and title unless
`tag` supplies a different name. For example, `reports: {}` under
`remotes.github` registers a release named `reports` in the producer's
repository. `repo: research-team/study-results` sends the files to a
separate repository. A release such as `figures-main` can hold files from
several project versions.

| Destination field | Values and effect |
|---|---|
| `path` | Local archive path, relative to the project root or absolute. |
| `repo` | GitHub repository in `owner/repo` form. Defaults to the repository where the analysis is built. |
| `structure` | `archive` (default) stores versioned payloads. `latest` keeps the current payload for each label. |
| `path-append-label` | Defaults to true. On a local destination, false lays out artifacts without the label subdirectory. A dedicated path per label avoids overlapping payloads. |
| `tag` | GitHub release name, used for both the Git tag and the displayed release title. Defaults to the registered name. A literal `archive` shares one release across versions. |
| `branch` | Optional GitHub target branch for a new tag. The branch must exist in the destination repository. `@branch` selects the checkout's named branch. Reusing a release preserves its tag target. |
| `send.cue` | `if-change` (default) or `always`. |
| `send.inspect` | `manifest` (default) compares recorded hashes, `file` inspects the files themselves, and `none` treats the destination as empty for comparison. |
| `send.strategy` | `sync-diff` sends changes and removes obsolete files. `sync-purge` replaces the remote contents, `upload-all` sends every local file, and `upload-missing` sends only absent names. Defaults to `sync-diff`, or `upload-all` with `inspect: none`. |
| `source` | Set true to prefer this destination for restores, false to skip it, or list the labels for which it is preferred. |

In an older inline `build.github` entry, `title` can also supply the release
name. Under `remotes.github`, the mapping key names the destination and `tag`
sets the release name.

For a one-off production archive, pass labels to `archive_local` or
`archive_github`. `TRUE` chooses the available archive labels. `always_archive`
controls whether those one-off archives are sent even when unchanged.

### Naming a destination for a branch or build

Directory paths, local destination names and paths, and GitHub release names
can contain the following placeholders.

| Placeholder | Example |
|---|---|
| `@version` | `archive-@version` becomes `archive-v1.2.3` for build 1.2.3. |
| `@branch` | `archive-@branch` on `feature/foo` becomes `archive-feature_2ffoo`. A detached checkout uses `__detached-` followed by the full commit SHA. |
| `@uuid` | A fresh UUIDv4 for each build, shared by that build's scripts, renderers, paths and release operations. |

The build supplies the values for all three placeholders. For example,
`figures-@branch` uses the branch of the analysis being built even when the
release is hosted in a separate repository. The optional `branch` setting
selects the commit for a new GitHub tag in that destination repository.

Quote a YAML string that begins with `@`. A placeholder ends at the end of
the string or before a hyphen, underscore, period, ordinary space or path
separator. For instance, `"@branch/@version"` expands both tokens, and
`archive-@branching` stays literal. Ignore rules cover the configured path
template across runs.

### Archive layout and restore

Local destinations keep per-label histories under `manifests/`. GitHub
Releases carry those histories in a single `manifest.zip` alongside the
artifact ZIPs. In an archive structure, a GitHub artifact is named, for
example, `output-figures-v1.2.3.zip`. An empty directory version can have an
explicit empty marker. In a flat local latest destination the names
`manifests`, `manifest.csv`, `VERSION`, and `CHANGELOG.md` at its root belong
to projr.

To reproduce a checked-out build published to GitHub, run `projr_restore()`
in the checkout. It uses the release named `archive` by default and restores
the declared raw directory labels. It reads the checkout's production version,
or the most recent completed build in its `.projr/BUILDLOG.md` when on the follow-up
development commit. Supply `version = "1.2.3"` for a specific build or
`destination` for another release tag. It verifies every selected directory's
paths and MD5s before installing any downloads. Local changes and extra files
stop the restore unless you explicitly allow replacement with `clear = TRUE`.

In a checkout with manifest history, run `projr_content_update()` to restore
the raw labels. Supply `label` to restore other directories. Projr first
considers a directory's configured `source` and then eligible build
destinations. Use `pos = "source"` or `"dest"` to limit the search, `type` to
select local or GitHub, and `title` to select the configuration entry.
Within the selected destination, restore chooses its latest available version
for the label. `clear = TRUE` can remove existing local files, including when
the archive records an empty version.

If a destination contained `@uuid`, find its concrete path or release tag in
the **Resolved archive destinations** section of that build's `.projr/BUILDLOG.md`.
In an older checkout, projr can read a root `BUILDLOG.md`. The next build
or restore moves that history into `.projr/`. The changelog stays at the root.
Pass it back as `destination` to restore from the same place later.

```r
projr::projr_content_update(
  label = "output-delivery", pos = "dest", type = "local", title = "shared",
  destination = "../team-archives/study"
)
```

`projr_restore_repo("owner/repo")` clones a repository and restores its
artifacts. Use `projr_restore_repo_wd("owner/repo")` to clone into the current
directory. Both accept the same label, source and destination selectors.
